Thought: I need to determine the backbone structure of siloxanes. Siloxanes are compounds that contain silicon-oxygen bonds in their backbone structure. Let me recall the structure of siloxanes.

Siloxanes have a backbone structure consisting of alternating silicon and oxygen atoms, which can be represented as -Si-O-Si-O-. This is different from:
- Carbon-based backbones (-C-C-C-) as in option A
- Ethers or polyethers (-C-O-C-O-) as in option B
- Silanes (-Si-Si-Si-) as in option D
